summary: The most successful videos have engaging hooks, focus on psychology and money, and are concise, with viewers dropping off significantly in slower-paced or less relevant content. The worst-performing videos often have weaker hooks, meander in the middle, or fail to keep viewers engaged throughout, suggesting a need for tighter scripting and more compelling topics.
script_tips: Craft hooks that immediately grab attention, ideally with a provocative statement or question that sets up the rest of the video.
Maintain a brisk pace, especially in the first 10% of the video, to prevent early drop-offs and keep viewers engaged.
Keep videos concise, aiming for lengths under 2 minutes, as longer videos tend to see significant drop-offs unless they are exceptionally engaging.
End videos with a call to action, a thought-provoking question, or an encouragement to like and subscribe to increase engagement and retention.
topic_tips: Focus on topics related to psychology, money, and personal development, as these seem to resonate most with the audience.
Use titles that include numbers or specific benefits (e.g., '5 Sneaky Supermarket Mind Tricks') to pique interest and make the content more accessible.
Explore topics that offer actionable advice or insights, such as 'body language hacks' or 'conversation starters', as these provide tangible value to viewers.

videos.title: The Placebo Effect: They Got Drunk on Drinks With Zero Alcohol
videos.hook: Why does a glass of water taste like vodka when you think it does?
videos.topic: The placebo effect: people got drunk on drinks with zero alcohol. Real study: in 2003 Seema Assefi and Maryanne Garry (published in Psychological Science) gave 148 students plain tonic water; half were told it was vodka and tonic. The tonic was poured from real vodka bottles and the glass rims were wiped with limes dipped in vodka. The 'vodka' group acted drunk, some showed physical signs of being drunk, and many insisted they had felt drunk when told the truth. They were also easier to mislead in a memory test, and more confident in their wrong memories. Lesson: what you believe changes how you act, so your beliefs about yourself (confidence, money, ability) work the same way. Do not claim they slurred their words || Title: The Placebo Effect: They Got Drunk on Drinks With Zero Alcohol
